title: Sample Paper: Sparse Attention Routing for Long-Context Language Modeling
abstract: We introduce a sparse attention routing scheme that scales linearly in sequence length while retaining 98% of full-attention quality on language modeling and reading comprehension. The router predicts query-aware key selection masks at each layer.

sections.heading: Introduction
paragraphs: Full self-attention scales quadratically. Existing sparse variants either use fixed patterns or learn routing in coarse blocks.
Our contribution is a per-token gating network that scores keys in O(L log L) and selects the top-k for attention.

sections.heading: Method
paragraphs: We replace the dense softmax attention with a routed attention where each query selects k=64 keys from the cache.
The router is a 2-layer MLP shared across heads; routing scores are made differentiable via Gumbel-top-k.

sections.heading: Experiments
paragraphs: We pretrain a 350M-parameter model on the Pile and evaluate on LAMBADA and SCROLLS.
Our model matches full-attention perplexity within 0.2 nats while reducing memory by 6.4x at 8k context.

sections.heading: Limitations
paragraphs: Routing quality degrades when k<32; we did not test contexts longer than 16k.

citations.raw: Tay et al., Long Range Arena, 2021.
